claims.statement: Impaired junction relaxation with premature or failed swallows throughout supports spastic achalasia when normal peristalsis is absent.
claims.limitation: Requires adequate acquisition and secondary-cause assessment. Observations use laboratory-relative measurements.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: CCv4 section 6.1

claims.statement: Opioid-associated spastic motor findings warrant assessment off opioids when clinically feasible.
claims.limitation: Conditional consensus. Adjustment requires the prescribing team. No fixed interruption interval or guaranteed reversibility.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: CCv4 section 6.3

claims.statement: Symptomatic EGJ outflow-obstruction physiology with retained peristalsis requires corroborating obstruction evidence from timed barium testing or FLIP for a clinically conclusive diagnosis.
claims.limitation: A manometric category does not establish a treatment indication. Supportive test choice remains contextual.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: CCv4 section 7.1 and ACG barium/FLIP sections

claims.statement: Failed peristalsis with relaxation measurements at the upper normal limit can leave achalasia unresolved and justify complementary testing in dysphagia.
claims.limitation: Device-specific limits and adequate testing matter. This is an inconclusive pattern.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: CCv4 sections 6.2-6.3

claims.statement: FLIP can evaluate obstructive motor physiology when manometry remains incomplete despite assisted placement.
claims.limitation: FLIP does not recreate a complete HRM subtype. No numeric distensibility threshold or universal hierarchy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG physiology key concept 4 and ACG achalasia FLIP section

claims.statement: A standardized upright timed barium examination assesses esophageal clearance.
claims.limitation: Individual series are constructed and interpreted with symptoms and anatomy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG physiology key concepts and Seoul statement 7

claims.statement: A barium tablet can add evidence about junction-level obstruction during esophagography.
claims.limitation: One directly checked guideline. No tablet-size or treatment cutoff authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG physiology barium recommendation 4

claims.statement: Reliable manometric interpretation depends on junction-crossing acquisition and an adequate separated-swallow protocol.
claims.limitation: Failed studies have several completion or complementary options.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: CCv4 standard protocol and ACG obstructive-symptom evaluation

claims.statement: Rapid-swallow recovery tests reserve, while solid-meal provocation can address symptoms unexplained by liquid swallows.
claims.limitation: No protocol recipe or claim that low reserve establishes junction obstruction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: CCv4 provocative maneuvers and ACG HRM sections

claims.statement: Weight loss and a suspicious junction-wall finding can warrant targeted structural assessment despite achalasia-pattern pressure findings.
claims.limitation: Supports investigation. Mucosal sampling can leave a deeper target unresolved.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG diagnostic testing and Seoul endoscopic assessment

claims.statement: SAGES favors POEM over Heller myotomy with fundoplication for adult type III achalasia.
claims.limitation: SAGES preference is expert opinion. ACG also accepts tailored Heller myotomy. Exact candidate ranking requires clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: SAGES KQ1 and ACG type III treatment discussion

claims.statement: Spastic achalasia can require a myotomy tailored to the involved esophageal-body segment.
claims.limitation: Extent is patient-specific. No fixed length or operative recipe.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG subtype/POEM sections and Seoul POEM discussion

claims.statement: POEM with appropriate reflux management and Heller myotomy with fundoplication are conditional alternatives for adult type I or II achalasia.
claims.limitation: Newer SAGES conditionally favors POEM over dilation. A universal winner is withheld.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: SAGES KQ1-KQ2 and ACG comparisons

claims.statement: Adding fundoplication to Heller myotomy reduces distal acid exposure, and a partial wrap is an accepted adjunct.
claims.limitation: Dor and Toupet remain accepted. These two partial wraps are not compared in the candidate.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG recommendations 7-8 and Seoul statement 16

claims.statement: A complete Nissen wrap after Heller myotomy can increase dysphagia compared with a partial Dor wrap.
claims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline synthesis of a randomized comparison.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: Seoul statement 16 discussion

claims.statement: Botulinum toxin is an accepted initial symptom-relief option when achalasia patients cannot undergo definitive junction therapies.
claims.limitation: Benefit is often temporary. Selection depends on procedural and rescue risk.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG recommendation 4 and Seoul statement 10

claims.statement: Pneumatic dilation requires perforation-rescue planning and suitability for surgery if repair is needed.
claims.limitation: One directly checked guideline supports this precise rescue boundary. No probability authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG pneumatic dilation section

claims.statement: Timed barium esophagography is the ACG first-line objective assessment for persistent or recurrent symptoms after definitive achalasia treatment.
claims.limitation: ACG names the first-line role. Seoul independently supports outcome assessment. Other findings remain complementary.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG recommendation 17 and Seoul statement 7

claims.statement: Recurrent symptoms after myotomy can arise from residual obstruction, altered anatomy, reflux injury or persistent motor dysfunction.
claims.limitation: One directly checked guideline. Symptoms do not establish which mechanism is active.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG post-therapy/failed-therapy sections

claims.statement: Post-POEM symptoms require objective assessment because reflux and impaired-clearance symptoms can overlap.
claims.limitation: Endoscopy and clearance findings answer complementary questions.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: SAGES KQ1 and ACG post-therapy assessment

claims.statement: Objectively confirmed reflux after POEM can be treated with a proton-pump inhibitor.
claims.limitation: No dose or duration authored. Candidate scores apparent myotomy failure and needs GERD boundary coordination.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: SAGES KQ1 and ACG treatment algorithm

claims.statement: Heller myotomy can be considered before esophagectomy after failed dilation and POEM when anatomy is favorable and prior myotomy is incomplete.
claims.limitation: Exact ACG sequencing rests on small heterogeneous case series. Seoul supports salvage possibilities without a universal ranking.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG recommendation 19 and Seoul recurrence section

claims.statement: Fit patients with severe distortion, disabling retention and prior-treatment failure may require high-volume-center esophagectomy assessment.
claims.limitation: Comprehensive individualized assessment remains necessary. No diameter mandates resection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG end-stage/recommendation 19 discussion and Seoul esophagectomy section

claims.statement: Achalasia treatment reduces junction resistance while loss of normal motor function can persist.
claims.limitation: Improved relaxation does not establish normal bolus emptying.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in outpatient foregut assessment or clinic review of outside treatment records.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG treatment goals and Seoul disease definition

claims.statement: Ambulatory reflux monitoring evaluates reflux burden and symptom association during a focused reflux assessment.
claims.limitation: Study preparation and exact interpretation depend on whether reflux is already proven. No protocol or cutoff is added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing esophageal symptom assessment.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG physiology esophageal reflux symptom section

claims.statement: PPI use and administration should be optimized before escalating treatment for persistent reflux symptoms.
claims.limitation: One directly verified primary guideline supplies this optimization step. The constructed record establishes current use and injury without assigning a universal failure interval.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment of post-myotomy symptoms or appropriate esophageal testing.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG refractory GERD recommendation 1 and optimization discussion

claims.statement: Conventional delayed-release daily PPI therapy is administered before the first meal to improve acid control.
claims.limitation: Single adequate source for meal-related administration. No dose amount or exact minute interval is authored in the question. This excludes meal-independent PPI formulations.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment of post-myotomy symptoms or appropriate esophageal testing.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG PPI medical therapy and optimization sections

claims.statement: Selected patients with persistent nocturnal reflux during optimized PPI use may benefit from as-needed bedtime H2-receptor blockade.
claims.limitation: Single guideline and limited data. Routine add-on therapy and sustained nightly efficacy are not asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment of post-myotomy symptoms or appropriate esophageal testing.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG H2RA taken at bedtime section

claims.statement: Famotidine blocks histamine H2 receptors and reduces gastric acid secretion.
claims.limitation: Drug-class identity only. The dictionary does not establish a regimen, a dose or its position in treatment sequencing.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment of post-myotomy symptoms or appropriate esophageal testing.
claims.verificationLocator: NCI Drug Dictionary famotidine entry

claims.statement: Endoscopy can evaluate reflux injury and luminal narrowing when symptoms recur after achalasia treatment.
claims.limitation: One directly checked guideline supports this complementary role. The current comparison uses its first-line timed-barium recommendation for recurrent retention-like symptoms.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment of post-myotomy symptoms or appropriate esophageal testing.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG diagnostic testing and post-therapy assessment

claims.statement: EUS can contribute to evaluation of a suspected infiltrative junction process when the clinical or imaging record raises that concern.
claims.limitation: One directly checked guideline. No universal EUS-versus-FLIP ordering is asserted for unexplained dysphagia.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment of post-myotomy symptoms or appropriate esophageal testing.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG achalasia diagnostic testing and pseudoachalasia discussion

claims.statement: When twice-daily conventional PPI therapy is selected, administration before breakfast and dinner is used; escalation follows assessment of persistent disease despite optimized daily therapy.
claims.limitation: Targeted ACG GERD guideline verification. This claim does not specify a universal duration, dose or automatic escalation for every persistent symptom.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment of post-myotomy symptoms or appropriate esophageal testing.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG GERD 2022 PPI optimization and persistent-symptom management discussion

withheldDisagreements.boundary: New SAGES conditional POEM preference and older multi-option guidance do not establish a universal type I/II key.
SAGES considers routine endoscopy by expert opinion and lacks validated intervals. ACG discourages routine cancer surveillance. The goals differ and no universal schedule is keyed.
No universal rescue ranking established. Candidates use incomplete myotomy versus distorted unobstructed-reservoir findings.
A current rights-checked isolated DES/hypercontractile treatment hierarchy was not established. This remains a research gap.

conceptMappings.identityReason: The retained draft chooses the next acquisition during opioid exposure. This version interprets an acquired off-medication response and decides whether the existing myotomy referral remains supported.
conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

conceptMappings.learningObjective: Use clearance and mucosal findings to choose treatment for symptoms mistakenly attributed to recurrent outflow obstruction.
conceptMappings.identityReason: This consequence-of-myotomy construct distinguishes objective inflammation with adequate clearance from recurrent junction obstruction. Coordinate its boundary with the GERD worker.
conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

conceptMappings.learningObjective: Integrate documented outflow physiology and procedural rescue risk when selecting initial symptom relief.
conceptMappings.identityReason: No assigned variant tests why an apparently less invasive pneumatic dilation can remain unsuitable when perforation rescue is prohibitive.
conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

conceptMappings.learningObjective: Distinguish a retained-peristalsis pressure pattern from conclusive achalasia and choose a complementary obstruction assessment.
conceptMappings.identityReason: Existing EGJOO appears as a diagnostic foil. This new construct scores the additional evidence needed to establish its clinical relevance.
conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

conceptMappings.learningObjective: Choose complementary distensibility assessment after genuine repeated inability to complete pressure testing.
conceptMappings.identityReason: The live acquisition questions favor assisted completion. This new boundary asks what to do after assistance has also failed to produce usable measurements.
conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

conceptMappings.learningObjective: Avoid closing the achalasia assessment from an upper-normal relaxation value when all body contractions fail.
conceptMappings.identityReason: Assigned recognition variants use clearly elevated relaxation pressures. This new decision concerns unresolved outflow obstruction when the measured pressure is at the upper normal boundary.
conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

conceptMappings.learningObjective: Use residual junction obstruction and favorable anatomy to consider Heller salvage before esophagectomy.
conceptMappings.identityReason: No assigned item tests organ-preserving salvage after endoscopic treatment failure with evidence of an incomplete myotomy.
conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

conceptMappings.learningObjective: Recognize severe anatomic reservoir failure after adequate junction therapies and select a high-volume esophageal-center referral.
conceptMappings.identityReason: This distinct later construct scores the boundary where severe reservoir failure persists despite a completed myotomy and further junction treatment lacks a demonstrated target.
conceptMappings.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

This version adds a distinct medication-use decision: optimize an actually acquired daily PPI administration pattern before escalation. Preserve v1 and its history separately.

revisionDispositions.reason: The completed symptom and physiologic recovery fairly supports deferral, but leaves neither offered junction procedure a credible present competitor. Wording repairs do not make this a difficult two-step decision. No accepted basic-purpose exception exists; changing the acquired response would replace the clinical problem.

Removing the unique tailored qualifier and representing comparable body-plus-junction myotomy coverage leaves a legitimate tailored Heller alternative. Current SAGES preference is expert opinion, while ACG accepts tailored POEM or Heller. The represented anatomy does not independently establish a unique patient-specific ranking; do not invent a coverage cutoff or local permission to select POEM.

Replaced the redundant adequate-manometry repeat with endoscopy, a distinct plausible investigation for post-treatment mucosal injury or stricture. Re-solved TBE versus endoscopy and reflux monitoring for recurrent food hold-up; all choices occupy the same diagnostic stage and later results remain hidden.

Removed the supplied esophagitis diagnosis, retained raw clearance and mucosal observations, supplied actual current medicine use, and replaced excluded junction procedures with three reflux-medicine regimens. The closest competitor is twice-daily PPI escalation, separated by unoptimized current administration.
Exact editorial PASS version preserved; clinical approval remains separate.

Used a complete neutral persistent-dysphagia task. Replaced routine repeated liquid-swallow manometry with a distinct standardized solid-meal extension. Feedback now explains why preserved propagation plus elevated outflow pressures remains clinically inconclusive without accepted supportive obstruction evidence.

Retained genuine failed acquisition after assisted crossing. Replaced both repeated investigations with new EUS and pH-impedance alternatives. The comparison now requires choosing a physiologic assessment over structural-wall or reflux assessment, rather than choosing the only untried test. Marked this advanced and narrower in yield.
Exact editorial PASS version preserved; clinical approval remains separate.

revisionDispositions.compositionHold: The PASS first node has empty terminal dispositions in its reviewed paired context. Removing its parked companion would alter that exact node. Preserve the complete reviewed case and withhold this pair from active preview pending manager composition review.

revisionDispositions.reason: After repairing chronology and referral-label symmetry, both repeat outlet procedures still lack a target at the widely patent junction. Prior salvage feedback also scaffolds the reservoir-versus-outlet distinction. The supported facts do not supply a credible different remaining strategy with a defensible single-best ranking; retain the fair observations and park the easy comparison.
